definition: The length of time that something lasts, continues, or remains in effect.

mnemonic.root_memory: DUR connects to "to last", which supports the core meaning of duration.
mnemonic.story_en: Remember DURATION by linking the root idea to a real academic or professional situation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用字根聯想到 DURATION 的核心意思，放進學術或職場語境中記憶。

example: The duration of the trial depends on how quickly the court reviews the evidence.
example_zh: 審判期間取決於法院審查證據的速度。

near_synonyms.difference: period names a stretch of time; duration stresses how long it lasts.

usage_note: duration is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: Changing, active, and full of movement or interaction; also relating to forces that produce motion.

mnemonic.story_en: Remember DYNAMIC by linking the root idea to a real academic or professional situation.

example_zh: 線上市場是動態的，因此公司必須快速回應需求變化。

near_synonyms.difference: changing simply means becoming different; dynamic suggests active forces and interaction.
flexible means able to adapt; dynamic means actively changing.

usage_note: dynamic is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To make it possible for someone or something to do something by providing tools, conditions, or permission.

mnemonic.root_memory: EN connects to "to make", which supports the core meaning of enable.

near_synonyms.difference: allow means permit; enable means make possible or provide ability.

usage_note: enable is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To meet, experience, or face someone or something unexpectedly or as part of a process.

near_synonyms.difference: organization is a group structure; entity can be any distinct thing that exists.

usage_note: entity is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To create, start, or prove something so that it becomes accepted, stable, or official.

definition: To go beyond a limit, expectation, number, or standard.

example_zh: 申請人數超過大學原本的估計。

near_synonyms.difference: surpass often implies doing better; exceed simply means go beyond a limit.

usage_note: exceed is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To deliberately leave someone or something out, or prevent entry or participation.

mnemonic.root_memory: EX connects to "out", which supports the core meaning of exclude.
mnemonic.story_en: Remember EXCLUDE by linking the root idea to a real academic or professional situation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用字根聯想到 EXCLUDE 的核心意思，放進學術或職場語境中記憶。

example_zh: 分析從最終資料集中排除了不完整回覆。

mnemonic.story_zh: 用字根聯想到 EXECUTE 的核心意思，放進學術或職場語境中記憶。

example: The team executed the marketing strategy across three regional markets.
example_zh: 團隊在三個區域市場執行了行銷策略。

near_synonyms.difference: implement means put into practice; execute stresses carrying out effectively.
perform is broad; execute can imply precision or authority.

usage_note: execute is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To show, display, or demonstrate a quality, behavior, object, or work of art.

definition: To become larger in size, amount, range, or influence, or to make something larger.

example_zh: 公司計畫將服務擴展到鄉村社區。

definition: To reveal something hidden or make someone or something experience a condition, influence, or risk.

definition: Located outside something, coming from outside, or related to outer conditions rather than inner ones.

definition: To remove, take out, or obtain something from a larger source, often by effort or a technical process.

mnemonic.story_en: Remember EXTRACT by linking the root idea to a real academic or professional situation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用字根聯想到 EXTRACT 的核心意思，放進學術或職場語境中記憶。

example: Researchers extracted key variables from thousands of medical records.
example_zh: 研究人員從數千份醫療紀錄中提取關鍵變項。

near_synonyms.difference: remove means take away; extract suggests taking out from within something.
derive means obtain from a source; extract often involves effort or separation.

usage_note: extract is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: A circumstance, element, or influence that contributes to a result or decision.

mnemonic.story_zh: 用字根聯想到 FACTOR 的核心意思，放進學術或職場語境中記憶。

definition: Related to a national government that shares power with state or regional governments.

mnemonic.root_memory: FOEDUS connects to "treaty, league", which supports the core meaning of federal.
mnemonic.story_en: Remember FEDERAL by linking the root idea to a real academic or professional situation.
mnemonic.story_zh: 用字根聯想到 FEDERAL 的核心意思，放進學術或職場語境中記憶。

mnemonic.story_en: Remember FLEXIBLE by linking the root idea to a real academic or professional situation.

example_zh: 早期測試揭露幾個薄弱假設後，研究人員改進了模型。

usage_note: Refine is common with method, model, design, argument, technique, and skill.

definition: The base on which something is built; also the underlying principle or organization that supports an activity.

mnemonic.root_memory: FUNDARE connects to "to lay a base", which supports the core meaning of foundation.
mnemonic.story_en: Remember FOUNDATION by linking the root idea to a real academic or professional situation.

near_synonyms.difference: rule emphasizes authority; govern can refer to political control or regulatory principles.

example_zh: 該研究找出影響學生動機的三個因素。

near_synonyms.difference: recognize means know when seen; identify often means name or establish specifically.

usage_note: identify is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

mnemonic.story_en: Remember IMPLICATION by linking the root idea to a real academic or professional situation.

near_synonyms.difference: enforce makes a rule obeyed; impose creates or places the rule or burden.

usage_note: impose is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.

definition: To look at something carefully in order to check its condition, quality, or compliance with rules.

usage_note: interact is common in academic, professional, or analytical English; use the collocations for natural phrasing.
